6 questions. Click an answer to check it: you will see right away whether it is correct, with a short explanation. Nothing is saved.

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="0"}
**1.** Which property must every linear transformation $T$ have?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- $T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v)$ and $T(kv) = k\,T(v)$
- $T(v)$ always has the same length as $v$
- $T(v) = v + b$ for a fixed vector $b$
- $T$ must go from $\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
Additivity and scaling. A consequence: a linear transformation always keeps the origin in place ($T(0) = 0$), so adding a fixed $b$ is **not** linear.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**2.** For a 2×2 matrix $A$, what is its first column?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- The determinant of $A$
- Where $A$ sends the basis vector $e_1 = [1, 0]$
- Where $A$ sends $e_2 = [0, 1]$
- An eigenvector of $A$
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
$A e_1$ is the first column and $A e_2$ the second. Knowing where $e_1$ and $e_2$ go tells you the whole transformation.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**3.** The shear $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0.5\\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ has determinant 1. What does it do to areas?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- Doubles them
- Keeps them unchanged
- Sets them to zero
- Flips their sign only
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
$|\det(A)|$ is the factor by which areas are scaled. A determinant of 1 means areas are preserved, even though the squares are tilted.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="2"}
**4.** A matrix has determinant 0. What happens?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- Nothing special
- It is a rotation
- The plane collapses onto a line (or a point): the matrix is not invertible
- Areas are doubled
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
The columns are collinear, so all of the plane is squeezed onto a line. That is why $Ax = b$ has no unique solution.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="2"}
**5.** Which transformation has **no** real eigenvector?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- Scaling the x-axis by 2
- Reflection about the y-axis
- Rotation by 90°
- The identity
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
An eigenvector keeps its direction. A 90° rotation turns **every** direction, so no real vector stays on its own line.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**6.** You apply $A$ first, then $B$. Which matrix does the whole thing?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- $AB$
- $BA$
- $A + B$
- Both $AB$ and $BA$, they are always equal
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
The matrix closest to the vector acts first: $B(Av) = (BA)v$. In general $AB \neq BA$: the order matters.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-score}
:::
